Maya.why: She laid the bottom edge steadily (36 dominoes) and her nudge closed a break that would have cut the fall short, and she held off stroke 2 as agreed. She never confirmed the lower-arm join she was watching, and her leadership was reactive rather than setting a sequence for the table.

Tom.why: He laid the tail from the wrong end, which forced a late redo that consumed most of the final ten minutes, and the tail was probably incomplete at the push. His repeated 'standing' calls ran ahead of reality and kept others waiting, and he asked for help only when the clock forced it. The body connected under others' work, but the fish's most identifying part was his, and it fell short.

Priya.why: She drew the outline, set the nose-to-tail plan and the join-check rule, laid the top edge cleanly, and caught the tail error, which is strong quality control and direction. She caught the error too late to avoid the redo, never reported the result of her top-join check, and didn't assign single owners for joins until late, so her leadership is good in intent but incomplete in execution.

Leo.why: His top fin and lower arm are the only placements attributed to him, and his 6:45 inspection was the most specific of the table, naming the open arm tips and asking for a call. He called the top fin down while the tail was still being laid and called the lower arm standing without a confirmed join, so his call-outs got ahead of what was on the table, and he stepped up to lead only where he saw a gap.
